section_summary: This section tracks Japanese merchant ships and naval vessels through East and Southeast Asian, Pacific, and South American ports in late 1941. It includes reports on cargoes, possible military equipment, bunkering, and ships under Japanese operation, followed by 1942 correspondence about the last Japanese vessels to reach United States ports. Several telegrams are accompanied by corrected copies or forms relaying their contents to the Navy.

subfiles.title: Antofagasta departure report
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese ship's departure from Antofagasta with mineral cargo.
subfiles.summary: A ship departed for Tocopi with 1,280 tons, mostly lead-silver and antimony.

subfiles.title: Arrival of Peian at Shanghai
subfiles.about: Reports the arrival of the Japanese-operated Peian.
subfiles.summary: Peian arrived at Shanghai from Port Campha on November 22.

subfiles.title: Peian arrival relayed to Navy
subfiles.about: Relays Stanton's report of Peian's arrival at Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Records Peian's November 22 arrival from Port Campha.

subfiles.title: Corrected Peian arrival telegram
subfiles.about: Corrects the report of Peian's arrival from Port Campha.
subfiles.summary: Peian, Japanese operated, arrived at Shanghai on November 22.

subfiles.title: Second corrected Peian arrival copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the corrected report of Peian's arrival.
subfiles.summary: Peian arrived from Port Campha on November 22.

subfiles.title: Corrected Peian arrival Navy relay
subfiles.about: Supplies a corrected Navy relay concerning Peian.
subfiles.summary: Records Peian's November 22 arrival at Shanghai and notes transmission to Navy on December 8.

subfiles.title: Peian sails for Hongay
subfiles.about: Reports Peian's departure for Hongay.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese-operated Peian sailed on December 1.

subfiles.title: Peian departure relayed to Navy
subfiles.about: Relays Peian's sailing from Shanghai to Hongay.
subfiles.summary: Records the December 1 departure and Navy transmission.

subfiles.title: Saigon and Haiphong vessel movements
subfiles.about: Reports merchant and destroyer movements in Saigon and Haiphong.
subfiles.summary: Ganges Maru arrived at Saigon; Hakibasan Maru departed for Yokohama, and a second Japanese destroyer arrived.

subfiles.title: Saigon and Haiphong movements relayed to Navy
subfiles.about: Relays Browne's merchant and destroyer movement report.
subfiles.summary: Lists Ganges Maru, Hakibasan Maru, and a Japanese destroyer; reports no Haiphong movements through November 29.

subfiles.title: Japanese diplomats arriving at Acapulco
subfiles.about: Points to another file concerning Japanese diplomats arriving aboard a vessel.
subfiles.summary: References McGurk's October 7 despatch on diplomats arriving at Acapulco.

subfiles.title: Immunity claims for Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: Points to correspondence accepting immunity claims for three Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: References immunity claims for Tatuta Maru, Kikawa Maru, and Taiyo Maru.

subfiles.title: Saigon and Haiphong departures
subfiles.about: Reports merchant vessel departures and Japanese warship movements.
subfiles.summary: Hukuz yu Maru left Haiphong and Ganges Maru left Saigon; two destroyers departed Saigon and a cruiser arrived.

subfiles.title: Saigon and Haiphong departures relayed to Navy
subfiles.about: Relays Browne's report of departures and Japanese warships.
subfiles.summary: Lists Ganges Maru and Hukuz yu Maru departures and notes the destroyers and cruiser.

subfiles.title: No ship movements through December 2
subfiles.about: Reports no ship movements through December 2.
subfiles.summary: A separate Saigon telegram reports no movements.

subfiles.title: No-movements report relayed to Navy
subfiles.about: Relays Browne's no-movements report.
subfiles.summary: States that no ships moved through December 2.

subfiles.title: Japanese-crewed trawlers leave Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Reports the sudden departure of two Argentine-flagged, Japanese-crewed trawlers.
subfiles.summary: Presidente Roca and Presidente Mitre departed Buenos Aires. Their Japanese crews might include naval reservists; the vessels reportedly had a 15,000-mile range.

subfiles.title: Trawler report relayed to OPNAV
subfiles.about: Relays Armour's warning about two Argentine-flagged trawlers.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the trawlers' departure, Japanese crews, possible naval reservists, and checked report of a 15,000-mile cruising radius.

subfiles.title: Reported Tatuta Maru sailing
subfiles.about: Asks for confirmation of an unverified Tatuta Maru itinerary.
subfiles.summary: Customs reported a possible Yokohama–Los Angeles–Panama voyage and requested definite information.

subfiles.title: Toa Maru gold cargo at Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Reports a shipment of gold carried by Toa Maru.
subfiles.summary: Toa Maru arrived at Buenos Aires on October 15 with 73 cases of gold shipped from Tokyo to K. Kuwabara.

subfiles.title: Urgent orders concerning Terukawa Maru
subfiles.about: Passes on British Admiralty information about Terukawa Maru.
subfiles.summary: Two cables from Japan reportedly ordered the ship's dispatch hurried.

subfiles.title: Taiyo Maru passenger and vessel report
subfiles.about: Summarizes passenger statements and observations of Taiyo Maru at Honolulu.
subfiles.summary: Passengers described conditions in Japan and expected war. The report notes eleven additional life rafts, an inexperienced crew, and Taiyo Maru's November 5 departure for Yokohama.

subfiles.title: Toa Maru as a possible auxiliary cruiser
subfiles.doc_type: naval intelligence report and duplicate copy
subfiles.about: Assesses Toa Maru's route, loading, plating, and alleged weapons fittings.
subfiles.summary: After Toa Maru reached Callao, informants described heavy plating, gun foundations, antennas, and possible torpedo tubes. The naval attaché inspected it from the dock, estimated thinner plating than reported, and could not confirm torpedo tubes or board the ship.

subfiles.title: Restrictive-file routing sheet
subfiles.about: Records restricted handling and filing.
subfiles.summary: Mostly stamps and routing marks; substantive text is illegible.

subfiles.title: Tatuta Maru at Honolulu
subfiles.about: Reports Tatuta Maru's arrival and departure times.
subfiles.summary: Tatuta Maru arrived from Yokohama on October 23 and left for San Francisco on October 24.

subfiles.title: Japanese ships bound for the American coast
subfiles.about: Relays a report that Japanese sailings for the American coast would cease.
subfiles.summary: No more Japanese ships were reportedly to leave Japan for this coast.

subfiles.title: Formerly Japanese-chartered German ships
subfiles.about: Points to a report locating German merchant ships formerly under Japanese charter.
subfiles.summary: References a Navy report on ships bearing Japanese names.

subfiles.title: File and handwritten note
subfiles.about: Contains a file stamp and a largely illegible handwritten note.
subfiles.summary: The readable fragments refer to radio operations, merchant ships, and nationality.

subfiles.title: Gold carried by Toa Maru and another Japanese vessel
subfiles.about: Reports additional gold cargoes carried to South American ports.
subfiles.summary: A confidential source says Toa Maru retained gold for Brazil after unloading at Buenos Aires; another vessel brought gold to Callao.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about the last cargo vessel from Japan
subfiles.from: G. Kearns, Daniel F. Young, Inc.
subfiles.about: Requests the name and sailing date of the last ship carrying cargo from Japan to the United States in 1941.
subfiles.summary: The firm cites Tatuta Maru's July voyage and asks for help because Japanese steamship company records were unavailable.

subfiles.title: Reply about the last Japanese vessel
subfiles.from: Thomas Burke, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Answers the inquiry about the last Japanese vessel to arrive in a U.S. port.
subfiles.summary: The Department identifies Syoyo Maru, arriving in ballast at San Francisco on August 16, as the apparent last arrival and suggests asking the Navy for more.

subfiles.title: Japanese vessel movements in the American republics
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese vessel movements and fuel oil supply in Latin American ports.
subfiles.summary: No future sailings from Japan or vessels en route to Latin America were reported. The memorandum lists recent movements of Naruto Maru, Terukawa Maru, Azuma Maru, and Toa Maru. It identifies Zorritos and Manzanillo as principal bunkering ports and describes Peru's limits on fuel supplied to Japanese ships.

subfiles.title: Atago Maru's reported location
subfiles.about: Relays the Navy's assessment of Atago Maru's location.
subfiles.summary: Atago Maru sailed from Los Angeles for Yokohama on March 5, 1941; the Navy believed it was in Far Eastern waters.
